name: Multiple Large Deposits Followed by Immediate Large Withdrawals
canonical_name: Multiple Large Deposits Followed by Immediate Large Withdrawals

description: A transaction pattern where a customer receives multiple large deposits into their account and then immediately withdraws or transfers out large sums. This pattern is indicative of potential money laundering activity, particularly layering or placement stages.
context: Multiple large deposits followed by immediate large withdrawals
required_action: Flag transaction pattern for review; escalate to compliance team

name: Frequent Transfers to Multiple Accounts or Jurisdictions
canonical_name: Frequent Transfers to Multiple Accounts or Jurisdictions
key: frequent transfers to multiple accounts or jurisdictions|WARNING_SIGN|banking.communications
description: A pattern of frequent fund transfers to multiple different accounts and/or transfers to accounts in multiple jurisdictions. This behaviour may indicate an attempt to obscure the origin or destination of funds across borders.
required_action: Investigate beneficiary accounts and jurisdictions; document rationale

name: Round-Number Transactions
description: Transactions conducted in exact round amounts such as £10,000 or £20,000 rather than natural transaction amounts. This pattern may indicate deliberate structuring to avoid reporting thresholds or to obscure the true nature of fund movements.
required_action: Review transaction context and customer justification

name: Transfers to High-Risk Countries
description: Fund transfers directed to countries designated as high-risk for money laundering, terrorism financing, or sanctions concerns. Such transfers require immediate investigation and potential escalation.
required_action: Verify beneficiary details; check sanctions lists; document business purpose

name: Transactions Inconsistent with Customer Profile
description: Financial transactions that deviate significantly from the customer's known profile, occupation, income level, or historical transaction behaviour. This inconsistency may indicate account compromise, fraud, or illicit activity.
required_action: Contact customer to understand transaction purpose; update customer profile if appropriate

name: Pensioner Large Transfer to Shell Company in High-Risk Jurisdiction
canonical_name: Pensioner Large Transfer to Shell Company in High-Risk Jurisdiction
key: pensioner large transfer to shell company in high-risk jurisdiction|WARNING_SIGN|banking.communications
description: A specific high-risk scenario where a pensioner customer suddenly transfers a large sum (£50,000) to a shell company registered in a high-risk jurisdiction such as Panama. This pattern is highly inconsistent with typical pensioner profiles and suggests potential fraud, elder abuse, or money laundering.
context: A pensioner suddenly transferring £50,000 to a shell company in Panama
examples: Pensioner transferring £50,000 to shell company in Panama
required_action: Immediately escalate; verify legitimacy of beneficiary; assess potential fraud or money laundering risk

name: Reluctance to Provide Documentation
description: A customer exhibits unwillingness or resistance to supplying required identity, address, or beneficial ownership documentation during account opening or ongoing KYC verification. This is a key indicator of potential money laundering or account misuse.
required_action: Do not proceed with account opening; escalate to compliance team for review

name: Vague Account Purpose Statement
description: A customer is unable or unwilling to clearly articulate the legitimate business or personal purpose for opening or using the account. This vagueness prevents proper risk assessment and source of funds verification.
required_action: Request clarification; do not open account until clear purpose is documented

name: Inconsistent Transaction Purpose Narrative
description: A customer provides conflicting or changing explanations for the purpose or nature of transactions on their account. This inconsistency suggests potential deception or concealment of the true source or use of funds.
required_action: Investigate discrepancies; document all versions of narrative; escalate if inconsistencies cannot be resolved

name: Third-Party Proxy Use for Account Activity
canonical_name: Third-Party Proxy Use for Account Activity
description: A customer uses another person as an intermediary or proxy to conduct transactions on their account rather than conducting transactions directly themselves. This arrangement may indicate structuring, layering, or an attempt to obscure the beneficial owner.
examples: Friend withdraws funds on behalf of account holder
required_action: Verify authority and beneficial ownership; document proxy relationship; escalate if unauthorized or suspicious

name: Dormancy Following Large Deposit
description: A customer opens an account, makes a significant deposit, but then fails to use the account for its stated purpose or for normal banking activity. This pattern is consistent with money laundering placement and layering techniques.
context: Avoids using account normally after opening
Customer opens account, deposits £30,000, then has friend withdraw it
required_action: Monitor account; investigate source of funds and intended use; escalate if dormancy persists without explanation

name: Large Deposit Followed by Third-Party Withdrawal
canonical_name: Large Deposit Followed by Third-Party Withdrawal
description: A customer deposits a substantial sum into a newly opened account and then immediately arranges for a third party to withdraw the funds. This pattern is a classic indicator of money laundering, structuring, or account misuse to obscure beneficial ownership and fund origins.
context: Customer opens account, deposits £30,000, then has friend withdraw it
examples: Customer opens account, deposits £30,000, then has friend withdraw it
required_action: Freeze account pending investigation; file SAR if suspicious activity confirmed; escalate immediately

name: Money Services Business Activity

name: Art and Jewelry Dealer Business Activity

name: Used Car Dealership Business Activity

name: High-Value Goods Trade Business Activity

name: Staff Member

name: Large Cash Deposit Followed by Immediate Transfer Out
canonical_name: Large Cash Deposit Followed by Immediate Transfer Out

description: A suspicious transaction pattern where substantial cash is deposited and then immediately transferred out of an account, indicative of money laundering layering techniques. This red flag is exemplified by the Danske Bank case where £200B in suspicious money was allowed to flow through the system.
context: Danske Bank (AML Failure) - Issue: Allowed £200B suspicious money through
examples: £200B suspicious money flow through Danske Bank
required_action: Flag transaction for review; do not process until cleared

name: Unauthorized Account Creation Without Customer Consent
canonical_name: Unauthorized Account Creation Without Customer Consent
description: Staff creating accounts in customer names without proper authorization or customer knowledge. This misconduct signal was central to the Wells Fargo scandal where employees systematically opened unauthorized accounts to meet sales targets.

Why: Pressure to meet targets; ignored ethics
examples: Wells Fargo staff created fake accounts to meet sales targets
required_action: Immediately halt account creation; verify customer consent before any account opening

name: Unauthorized Data Sharing Without Customer Consent
canonical_name: Unauthorized Data Sharing Without Customer Consent
description: Sharing or transferring customer personal data to third parties without explicit customer consent or authorization. This data protection red flag resulted in the Facebook GDPR violation where user data was shared without proper consent mechanisms.
context: Facebook (GDPR Violation) - Issue: Shared user data without consent
Why: Didn't respect user data rights
examples: Facebook shared user data without consent
required_action: Do not share customer data; verify consent documentation before any disclosure
escalation_path: Data protection officer; compliance team; legal

name: Obligation to Report Suspicious Transactions
description: Staff must identify and report suspicious transactions to compliance authorities. Failure to fulfill this obligation, as demonstrated in the Danske Bank case, results in severe regulatory penalties and reputational damage.
context: Danske Bank (AML Failure) - Why: Staff ignored suspicious transactions
Consequence: €1B fine, CEO resigned, reputation destroyed
consequence_of_failure: Regulatory fines, reputational damage, loss of banking license, criminal prosecution of staff
regulatory_source: AML regulations; Danske Bank case demonstrates €1B fine consequence
verification_method: Transaction monitoring systems; staff training and audit

timeframe: before account creation or any account operation
consequence_of_failure: Regulatory fines, criminal prosecution, massive reputational damage, staff layoffs
regulatory_source: Consumer protection regulations; Wells Fargo case demonstrates $3B fine consequence

consequence_of_failure: Regulatory fines, ongoing investigation, reputational damage
